findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The BlockedEmail table ships completely inert: nothing in this diff writes to it except the fabricator in the spec directory. Site operators cannot populate blocked_emails through any UI, API endpoint, rake task, or seed, so the entire blocked-email feature added by this diff cannot be exercised in production until a follow-up writer exists — an admin who deploys this gets silently no protection.

[ADVISORY] should_block? performs a read-modify-write save (record.match_count += 1; record.save) inside a model validation, and it runs on every validation pass where the email changed. Any user creation attempt that fails for an unrelated reason (bad username, short password) still increments match_count and updates last_match_at for the attempted email, and Rails runs validations multiple times per request, so the match statistics this table exists to collect are inflated and unreliably reflect actual block events. Two concurrent signups with the same email also lose counter updates to the race between read and save.

[ADVISORY] record.save inside should_block? is invoked while the outer User validation is running, and its return value and validation errors are discarded. If the counter save fails (e.g., unique-index collision from a concurrent insert of the same email, or a database hiccup), the failure is swallowed with no logging, so operators get no signal that blocking statistics are being lost; a reviewer or auditor tracing match_count discrepancies will find no error trail.

[ADVISORY] The new errors and values keys in the create-failure JSON response have no test anywhere in the diff (the only new specs cover EmailValidator and BlockedEmail), and they are the contract the new client code in create_account_controller.js:274-276 depends on. A regression in the response shape (e.g., errors.to_hash keys, values payload) breaks the client-side rejectedEmails flow silently — the JS guard `result.errors && result.errors.email && result.values` just skips, and the blocked-email UX added by this diff stops working with no failing spec to catch it.

[ADVISORY] The whitelist/blacklist check in validate_each now only fires for User because it is gated behind `if: :email_changed?` on the model, and the file is missing a trailing newline (no `\ No newline` handling needed, but the file ends mid-token per the diff marker). Any future model that uses `validates :email, email: true` without the email_changed? guard gets the BlockedEmail DB hit and domain checks on every save of every record, a hot-path cost the current design hides; contributors reusing this validator copy the surprise. The missing newline also fails any repo-side lint/whitespace check on the new file.

[BUG] Nothing anywhere in this diff ever creates a BlockedEmail row — there is no admin UI, API endpoint, rake task, or seed path that writes to the blocked_emails table, so the 'block these users' feature ships inert. Site operators cannot use the feature at all: after deploy, no email can ever be blocked because the table stays empty; BlockedEmail.should_block? always returns false and the entire PR is dead code until some out-of-tree writer appears.

[BUG] The domain-restriction regex is built with `Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true)` and the BlockedEmail lookup uses `where(email: email)`, both case-sensitive against the local/whole address, so 'Bad@SpamClub.com' bypasses a block on 'bad@spamclub.com'. A blocked spammer re-registers with mixed-case email (e.g. 'BLOCK@spamfromhome.org') and passes validation; the block list is trivially bypassed by case variation, defeating the feature's core requirement.

[ADVISORY] The new response payload (`errors: user.errors.to_hash, values: user.attributes.slice(...)`) has no spec in the diff — the only test added is for the validator itself, and no existing spec is updated to assert these keys. If the payload shape drifts (e.g. `to_hash` keys or the `values` slice changes), the client-side `result.errors.email && result.values` gate in create_account_controller.js silently fails and the rejectedEmails UX regresses with no failing test; the diff's own spec directory (spec/controllers, spec/components) contains no UsersController#create test covering this.

[ADVISORY] The client-side rejectedEmails mechanism (pushObject on failure + accountInvalid rejection list) has no JS test, and the spec added in this diff only covers the Ruby validator. A regression in the property dependency (`rejectedEmails.@each`) or the pushObject guard leaves users with a server-side block they see only as a generic flash error; the invalid-inline-hint behavior this diff promises is unverified.

[ADVISORY] The whitelist/blacklist restriction logic was moved from User#email_validator into the new EmailValidator, but the new spec only covers the BlockedEmail.should_block? branch — no test exercises email_domains_whitelist or email_domains_blacklist through the new path. The migration of the restriction-setting logic is unverified: if `SiteSetting.email_domains_whitelist` behavior regressed in the move (e.g. because the `if: :email_changed?` condition now also gates restriction checks, whereas the old code ran `email_validator` under the same condition — but any change to `validate_each` argument handling), admins relying on domain restrictions get no failing spec.

[ADVISORY] The BlockedEmail check is skipped when the domain restriction already added an error (`record.errors[attribute].blank?`), so a blocked email that is also on the blacklist reports 'not allowed from that email provider' instead of 'blocked', and the blocked-email stats are never incremented. Admins loading the block table cannot distinguish which blocked emails attempted signups when both restriction settings and blocked_emails are in play — match_count and last_match_at silently undercount the actual blocked-attempt rate.

[ADVISORY] The blocked_emails feature ships with no writer anywhere in the diff — no admin UI, API endpoint, rake task, or seed path creates BlockedEmail records, so operators cannot populate the table the validator queries. Site operators who need to block email addresses have no way to do so; the entire BlockedEmail model, migration, and validator branch are dead code in production until an out-of-diff tool is written.

[BUG] The client rejects previously-failed emails with the generic I18n.t('user.email.invalid') message even when the server rejected the email with the specific 'user.email.blocked' reason, because the server error text is discarded in favor of a hardcoded client-side message. A user whose email was blocked by a moderator sees 'user.email.invalid' (implying a malformed address) instead of the distinct 'is not allowed' message the diff added, sending them on a futile hunt for a typo rather than telling them the address is disallowed.

[ADVISORY] BlockedEmail.should_block? performs a write (record.save) inside model validation, so every validation pass that reaches the email validator increments match_count and persists last_match_at as a side effect of a read-style check. Any code path that validates a User (admin screens, background jobs, spec fixtures calling .valid?) silently mutates blocked_emails rows; a failing save is also swallowed, so stats silently drift, and validators with DB writes make validation non-idempotent and unsafe inside transactions that roll back.

[ADVISORY] The BlockedEmail enforcement is gated on `if: :email_changed?`, so the blocked-email invariant is not enforced for any record whose email is unchanged — including users whose email was added before the block list existed or who never trigger a change during admin edits. Staff who block an email address after the fact will see existing accounts with that address continue to validate and save normally through any code path that doesn't change email, so the block list only gates signups/updates where the email field is dirty — an invariant gap not stated by the PR intent of 'comprehensive email validation for blocked users'.

[BUG] BlockedEmail#should_block? performs a read-modify-write on match_count (record.match_count += 1; record.save) with no atomic UPDATE, so concurrent requests both read the same count and one increment is lost. Two simultaneous signup attempts with the same blocked email both load count=N and both save N+1; match_count and last_match_at drift permanently downward relative to real match volume, and under Rails' stale-object save the whole row write can also clobber concurrent updates. Use update_all("match_count = match_count + 1") instead.

[BUG] The domain restriction logic (email_domains_whitelist/blacklist) was moved into EmailValidator but the blocked-email check is gated behind `record.errors[attribute].blank?`, meaning when a whitelist/blacklist error is added the should_block? side-effect is skipped, so the same email yields different match statistics depending on which restriction fires. Operators loading blocked_emails rows to audit 'has this email ever been blocked' (the exact use case the last_match_at spec comment describes) get silently missing match records for any email that also trips the domain restriction, because validation bails before the BlockedEmail lookup/write.

[BUG] should_block? mutates and saves a database row inside a model-validation callback chain, so every call to User#valid? — including multiple validations within one save, plus every retry after an unrelated error (bad username, short password) — re-runs the query and increments match_count. match_count/last_match_at are inflated multiple times per signup attempt and the record.save inside validation runs the full validation cycle again (and can fail silently), making the statistics columns unreliable for their stated purpose and coupling validation correctness to a DB write that can raise inside validate.

[BUG] BlockedEmail lookup is a case-sensitive exact string match (`where(email: email)`) with a case-sensitive unique index, so 'Spammer@X.com' bypasses a blocked 'spammer@x.com' record. A user whose email was blocked can register by changing the case of the local part or domain; the blocklist control is defeated by trivial case variation, and duplicate rows differing only in case are permitted by the unique index instead of collapsing to one canonical entry.

[ADVISORY] The blocked_emails table has no writer anywhere in the diff — no admin UI, API endpoint, rake task, or seed path inserts rows — so the entire blocking feature is inert until separate tooling ships. Operators cannot actually block an email address without hand-writing SQL; should_block? can never return true in production until the writer is added, and the migration deploys a table nothing populates.

[ADVISORY] The client pushes the email into rejectedEmails for ANY email error (uniqueness 'has already been taken', domain blacklist, blocked), and then displays the generic 'user.email.invalid' reason for all of them. A user whose email collides with an existing account (a potentially recoverable situation, e.g. they should log in instead) sees only 'invalid' with no actionable message, and the email is permanently marked rejected in the client for the session, forcing a page reload to retry even after fixing an unrelated field error.

[ADVISORY] The failure response now includes `errors: user.errors.to_hash` and `values: user.attributes.slice(...)`, but `email_validator`'s errors come from I18n while User also adds non-I18n messages (e.g. password_validator's hardcoded 'must be 6 letters or longer'), so the new errors hash mixes translated and untranslated strings with no structure the client can key on besides the attribute name. The client's only consumer of errors is `result.errors.email` presence, so any future decision logic or localization of the per-field message will have to re-derive error kinds from free-form strings; the API surface promises structured errors but delivers display strings.

[ADVISORY] Blocked emails are shown to the user with the generic 'user.email.invalid' message, discarding the server's distinct 'user.email.blocked' reason that this same diff adds. A user whose email is explicitly blocked sees 'invalid' rather than 'not allowed', and the new server-side locale string user.email.blocked is never surfaced in the client, so the messaging objective of the PR is silently half-implemented; users and support staff cannot distinguish blocked from malformed.

[ADVISORY] BlockedEmail.should_block? performs writes (incrementing match_count and updating last_match_at) inside model validation, so the statistics no longer measure blocks — they measure every validation attempt of a previously-blocked address. Any failed signup attempt that re-validates the same blocked email (wrong password, taken username, retry) inflates match_count, and last_match_at becomes 'last attempted' rather than 'last blocked', defeating the stated purpose of the last_match_at spec comment ("we can see whether those emails have ever been blocked").

[ADVISORY] The BlockedEmail check is skipped whenever any earlier error was added to :email (e.g. a uniqueness failure), so a blocked email that is also taken never gets recorded as blocked and never produces the blocked error. A user whose blocked email is also already registered sees only 'has already been taken' in full_messages, and because the client-side rejectedEmails gating depends on result.errors.email being present while the reason shown is the generic invalid string, the block semantics differ by which unrelated validation fires first.

[ADVISORY] The new EmailValidator retains the original ad-hoc regex domain restriction (including the re. escaping bug where '.' in a setting becomes '\\.' inside an unescaped group), so the review refactor moved the code but preserved an objective-critical behavior unchanged without any test covering the whitelist/blacklist paths — the new spec only covers BlockedEmail with the domain check stubbed out via SiteSetting being empty in tests. Any regression in the copied email_in_restriction_setting? logic (e.g. commas or regex metacharacters in the SiteSetting now behave differently than in the original method because it operates on the passed value rather than self.email) ships untested; sites relying on domain blacklists get no coverage from this diff.

[BUG] The validator spec stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? in every test, so the spec never exercises the validator's real integration with BlockedEmail — it verifies the stub, not the code path the diff ships. The guard `record.errors[attribute].blank? and BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` (email_validator.rb:16-18) is the only real logic tested, and only via a canned stub; the actual lookup/save side-effect inside should_block? running inside validation is never combined with the validator in any test, so a regression in how the validator invokes should_block? (wrong argument, wrong condition order) would surface only in production. BlockedEmail.should_block? IS covered separately in spec/models/blocked_email_spec.rb, but the composition is not — this is the specific assertion gap in the existing spec.

[BUG] The EmailValidator spec has zero tests for the whitelist/blacklist branch (email_validator.rb:5-13, email_in_restriction_setting?), even though that logic was moved from user.rb into this new class in this diff. The regex-building logic (`setting.gsub('.', '\.')`, case-insensitive Regexp with interpolated domain list) migrated from User#email_validator with no test; a regression in escaping or branch order (e.g. blacklist checked when whitelist present) would pass the entire suite. Checked spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb — both tests set neither SiteSetting, so `SiteSetting.email_domains_whitelist/blacklist` are empty in both and lines 5-13 never execute under test.

[BUG] The 'doesn't add an error' test is a false-confidence test: with SiteSettings empty and the stub returning false, the validator performs no operation that could ever add an error, so the test passes regardless of whether the validator's non-error logic is correct. The only thing this test could catch is the validator crashing on a nil/empty path; it asserts nothing about real behavior (no domain restriction is configured, BlockedEmail is stubbed to false). Combined with the stub-tautology above, the entire spec has at most one meaningful assertion (blocked -> error present), and even that only checks presence, not that the message is I18n 'user.email.blocked' vs 'not_allowed'.

[ADVISORY] The new client-side rejection state machine (rejectedEmails array, the emailValidation branch, the @each dependency, and the pushObject on server error) has no test anywhere in the diff and no existing JS spec was updated. Three behaviors are unverified: (1) a rejected email produces a failed validation with 'user.email.invalid' reason, (2) the property recomputes when rejectedEmails changes (the `@each` observer), and (3) pushObject only fires when `result.errors.email && result.values` are both truthy. A regression where the gating condition is wrong (e.g. server returns errors but no values) silently drops the block, and no test fails. Checked: no *.spec / *test* JS files appear in the diff referencing create_account_controller.

[ADVISORY] The new `errors:`/`values:` fields in the failed-create JSON response are asserted by no spec in the diff, and the JS consumer's shape assumption (`result.errors.email`, `result.values.email`) is likewise untested end-to-end. The client gates on `result.errors && result.errors.email && result.values` (create_account_controller.js:274-276); if the server payload shape drifts (e.g. errors serialized with a different key casing) the blocked-email UX silently degrades to the old generic flash and the block-list feature never populates. No controller spec in the diff pins this contract.

[BUG] BlockedEmail.should_block? performs a read-modify-write (record.save) inside model validation, so every validation attempt — including saves that fail for other reasons and repeated resubmissions of the same signup form — increments match_count and updates last_match_at. Statistics in blocked_emails are inflated and last_match_at is polluted by failed/aborted signup attempts, not actual block events; the write also runs inside what callers expect to be a pure validation pass (e.g. User.new(...).valid? in console/tests triggers DB writes), and races between concurrent validations lose match_count increments (last-write-wins on the stale read).

[BUG] BlockedEmail.where(email: email) matches case-sensitively while User emails are normalized to lowercase, so a blocked_emails row loaded with mixed-case (e.g. 'Spammer@Example.com', the only way to populate the table since this diff adds no writer) never blocks the corresponding user address. Operators who seed the table directly (there is no admin UI/rake path in this diff) get silent non-blocking for any row whose case doesn't exactly match the downcased user input.

[ADVISORY] The blocked_emails table ships with no writer anywhere in the diff — no admin UI, API endpoint, rake task, or seed path inserts rows, and no backfill migrates existing SiteSetting email_domains_blacklist entries into it. Operators cannot use the feature at all without hand-written SQL; the migration creates permanently empty infrastructure until a later PR, and existing blacklist configuration is not carried over so behavior silently relies on the fallback setting path.

[ADVISORY] The email domain whitelist/blacklist check now runs only when email_changed?, but EmailValidator is also a shared generic validator available to any model; combined with the removal of the model-local email_in_restriction_setting?, any existing code paths that relied on email domain restrictions being enforced on create with an unchanged/assigned email (e.g. mass-created or seeded users) skip the check entirely. Signup flows that set email via mass assignment then save (email_changed? true on create, so mostly safe) — but any later rework that reloads/assigns email outside change-tracking bypasses both the domain restriction and the BlockedEmail check, letting blacklisted-domain accounts through.

[BUG] should_block? does a read-modify-write (record.match_count += 1; record.save) with no error handling and no locking, so concurrent registrations of the same blocked email lose counter updates and a failed save is silently swallowed while still returning the block decision. Under concurrent requests two processes read the same match_count and both write count+1, losing increments; and if record.save fails (e.g. DB error, stale read under race) the failure is invisible — last_match_at/match_count statistics silently drift from reality, defeating the stated purpose of tracking whether a preloaded email has ever been blocked.

[BUG] The blocked-email lookup `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` is case-sensitive with no downcasing, so a user circumvents the block by varying the case of their address ("Bad@Spamclub.com" vs "bad@spamclub.com"). The blocked user this feature targets registers successfully by changing one letter's case; the validation path reports success (account created) for an address the operator explicitly blocked — the exact failure the feature exists to prevent.

[ADVISORY] The client adds the email to rejectedEmails for ANY server error on the email attribute (already-taken, not_allowed, blocked), and the emailValidation override then shows the generic 'user.email.invalid' message for that address even after the underlying condition changes. A user whose email fails with "has already been taken” or a transient provider-restriction error gets a permanent client-side rejection with the misleading "invalid" reason; if they later fix the server-side issue (account freed, admin clears restriction) and retype the same email, the client still refuses it until a full page reload, blocking a legitimate signup.

[ADVISORY] BlockedEmail.should_block? is only consulted when no whitelist/blacklist error was added, so on sites with email_domains_blacklist/whitelist configured, matches against preloaded blocked emails are never recorded and never blocked — the blocked-email feature silently no-ops. An operator who loads blocked_emails while also having a domain restriction setting gets zero blocking and zero match statistics from the new table with no warning; the account-creation path reports success for addresses they believed were blocked.

[ADVISORY] should_block? runs inside model validation, so a DB write to blocked_emails occurs on every save attempt where the email changed — including saves that fail for unrelated reasons (bad username, short password) and repeated retries. match_count and last_match_at inflate per failed retry rather than per registration attempt, so the statistics the model comment says operators will rely on ("we can see whether those emails have ever been blocked") overstate activity; also adds an unconditional write to the hot account-creation retry path.

goldens.comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.

The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

In `User` it is guarded by `if: :email_changed?`, but the validator itself is generic and could be applied elsewhere without that guard, causing those checks/DB hits on every validation — a valid reuse/architecture/perf concern grounded in `lib/validators/email_validator.rb` and `app/models/user.rb`. The note about the file ending mid-token is not supported (it ends with `end`), though the diff does show `\ No newline at end of file`, which is a minor whitespace/lint issue rather than a functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] BlockedEmail.where(email: email) matches case-sensitively while User emails are normalized to lowercase, so a blocked_emails row loaded with mixed-case (e.g. 'Spammer@Example.com', the only way to populate the table since this diff adds no writer) never blocks the corresponding user address. Operators who seed the table directly (there is no admin UI/rake path in this diff) get silent non-blocking for any row whose case doesn't exactly match the downcased user input.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `BlockedEmail.should_block?` does an exact-match lookup: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` (app/models/blocked_email.rb). Neither `EmailValidator` nor `BlockedEmail` normalizes the input (`value`) or stored emails (no downcasing/CI compare), so a blocked email stored with different casing than the user-provided email will not match on case-sensitive DBs (e.g., Postgres). This creates a bypass/silent non-blocking for mixed-case entries seeded directly into `blocked_emails`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The blocked_emails table ships with no writer anywhere in the diff — no admin UI, API endpoint, rake task, or seed path inserts rows, and no backfill migrates existing SiteSetting email_domains_blacklist entries into it. Operators cannot use the feature at all without hand-written SQL; the migration creates permanently empty infrastructure until a later PR, and existing blacklist configuration is not carried over so behavior silently relies on the fallback setting path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds the `blocked_emails` table/model and enforces it in `EmailValidator` via `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)`, but the diff contains no code path that creates/populates `BlockedEmail` rows (no controller/admin UI/seed/migration backfill). As a result, the new blocking capability is not operable from within the app based on this diff alone (it would require manual DB inserts). However, this is not a verifiable functional bug because existing domain whitelist/blacklist behavior is still implemented in `EmailValidator` and will work without any `blocked_emails` rows; the new table simply has no effect until populated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The email domain whitelist/blacklist check now runs only when email_changed?, but EmailValidator is also a shared generic validator available to any model; combined with the removal of the model-local email_in_restriction_setting?, any existing code paths that relied on email domain restrictions being enforced on create with an unchanged/assigned email (e.g. mass-created or seeded users) skip the check entirely. Signup flows that set email via mass assignment then save (email_changed? true on create, so mostly safe) — but any later rework that reloads/assigns email outside change-tracking bypasses both the domain restriction and the BlockedEmail check, letting blacklisted-domain accounts through.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show a regression where whitelist/blacklist checks newly “only” run on `email_changed?`: the pre-existing `User#email_validator` was already guarded by `if: :email_changed?` (`validate :email_validator, if: :email_changed?`), and the new validator usage preserves that same condition (`validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?`). On create, assigning an email will typically mark it changed, so the restriction checks still run. Claims about bypassing change-tracking via later rework or “unchanged/assigned email on create” are speculative and not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] should_block? does a read-modify-write (record.match_count += 1; record.save) with no error handling and no locking, so concurrent registrations of the same blocked email lose counter updates and a failed save is silently swallowed while still returning the block decision. Under concurrent requests two processes read the same match_count and both write count+1, losing increments; and if record.save fails (e.g. DB error, stale read under race) the failure is invisible — last_match_at/match_count statistics silently drift from reality, defeating the stated purpose of tracking whether a preloaded email has ever been blocked.

adjudication.rationale: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` (new in `app/models/blocked_email.rb`) performs a non-atomic read/modify/write (`record.match_count += 1; record.last_match_at = ...; record.save`) with no locking or atomic update. Under concurrent calls for the same email, two processes can read the same `match_count` and both write back `+1`, losing an increment. Additionally, it ignores the result of `record.save`, so failures to persist `match_count`/`last_match_at` are silently dropped while the method still returns the block decision based on `action_type`, causing the new tracking fields to drift from reality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The blocked-email lookup `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` is case-sensitive with no downcasing, so a user circumvents the block by varying the case of their address ("Bad@Spamclub.com" vs "bad@spamclub.com"). The blocked user this feature targets registers successfully by changing one letter's case; the validation path reports success (account created) for an address the operator explicitly blocked — the exact failure the feature exists to prevent.
matched_golden_ids: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same bypass risk: BlockedEmail.should_block?/lookup uses a case-sensitive email query without normalization, allowing differently cased emails to evade an existing block.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The client adds the email to rejectedEmails for ANY server error on the email attribute (already-taken, not_allowed, blocked), and the emailValidation override then shows the generic 'user.email.invalid' message for that address even after the underlying condition changes. A user whose email fails with "has already been taken” or a transient provider-restriction error gets a permanent client-side rejection with the misleading "invalid" reason; if they later fix the server-side issue (account freed, admin clears restriction) and retype the same email, the client still refuses it until a full page reload, blocking a legitimate signup.

adjudication.rationale: In `create_account_controller.js`, any failed signup response that includes `result.errors.email` causes the client to `pushObject(result.values.email)` into `rejectedEmails` (lines adding to `rejectedEmails` in the failure branch). Later, `emailValidation` immediately fails for any email contained in `rejectedEmails` and returns the generic `I18n.t('user.email.invalid')` (new early-return block), preventing re-validation/server submission for that same address during the lifetime of the controller. This is independent of the actual server-side reason (e.g., uniqueness, domain restriction, blocked), so it can permanently block a legitimately usable email after conditions change and also shows a misleading generic error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] BlockedEmail.should_block? is only consulted when no whitelist/blacklist error was added, so on sites with email_domains_blacklist/whitelist configured, matches against preloaded blocked emails are never recorded and never blocked — the blocked-email feature silently no-ops. An operator who loads blocked_emails while also having a domain restriction setting gets zero blocking and zero match statistics from the new table with no warning; the account-creation path reports success for addresses they believed were blocked.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmailValidator#validate_each`, `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` is only skipped when a prior email restriction error was added (`if record.errors[attribute].blank? and BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)`). However, the finding claims that on sites with `email_domains_whitelist/blacklist` configured, blocked emails are “never recorded and never blocked” and that account creation “reports success” for blocked addresses. The diff does not support that: if the email passes the whitelist/blacklist check (no error added), `should_block?` is still consulted and will block; if it fails the domain restriction, account creation would fail anyway (with `user.email.not_allowed`), not succeed. At most, match-count stats won’t be incremented when the email is already rejected for domain reasons, but the feature does not globally no-op under whitelist/blacklist settings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] should_block? runs inside model validation, so a DB write to blocked_emails occurs on every save attempt where the email changed — including saves that fail for unrelated reasons (bad username, short password) and repeated retries. match_count and last_match_at inflate per failed retry rather than per registration attempt, so the statistics the model comment says operators will rely on ("we can see whether those emails have ever been blocked") overstate activity; also adds an unconditional write to the hot account-creation retry path.

adjudication.rationale: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` performs a DB write (`match_count += 1`, `last_match_at = ...`, `save`) whenever a matching `blocked_emails` row exists (app/models/blocked_email.rb). This method is invoked from `EmailValidator#validate_each` during user validation (`validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?` in app/models/user.rb and lib/validators/email_validator.rb). Model validations run even when the save ultimately fails due to other attributes (e.g., username/password), so repeated failed retries with the same email will repeatedly increment `match_count`/update `last_match_at`, inflating these stats and adding extra writes on the account-creation retry path. This is a real diff-grounded concern (metrics/perf/semantics), but not a clearly verifiable functional break.
